evidence.note: Claim: a local reviewer service name (rev.name) and model (rev.model) leak into the committed event log because the log redactor's name pass does not know them. Probe: tests/test_log_redaction_reviewer_names.py appends a gate.failed event whose evidence carries a synthetic reviewer name+model and asserts neither reaches the shard. Result: before the fix the name lemma survived the shard (AssertionError: name reached the committed log); after adding reviewer name+model to the committed-log redactor's names the assertion passes. Refutation point: the name/model would still appear raw in the shard. Verdict: CONFIRMED.

Applied r-gemini-key-load context and the redaction contract (reviewer endpoints/model names/key variables stay local). ddflow core.redact layering honored: _eventlog builds the committed-log Redactor's names; the reviewer loader is imported lazily (services<->infra).

ddflow/infra/log/_eventlog.py adds _reviewer_redact_names (deferred load_reviewers, name+model) and extends the redactor names; ddflow/services/gates/reviewers.py _unapproved_reviewer reads the name from the reviewer.configured subject (verbatim) instead of the redacted evidence copy. Regression test tests/test_log_redaction_reviewer_names.py. 354 redaction+trust tests pass.

chunk_findings.detail: The name pass now treats every `load_reviewers` name and model as a redact token, including the `reviewer.configured` subject that `pending_reviewer_name` (ddflow/services/gates/reviewers.py) is changed to trust as verbatim. Given a configured reviewer `name = "local-reviewer-f8f8"`, appending `reviewer.configured` stores `[REDACTED:name]` in the shard; after replay `state.reviewer_writes[dig]["name"]` is that placeholder (or missing), and the new `return str(name or evidence["reviewer"])` hands the gate a redacted identity, so the pending local reviewer no longer matches. The same pass also strips public reviewers: `name = "gemini"` / `model = "gemini-2.5-flash"` disappears from later shards, not only the git-ignored local layer.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/log/_eventlog.py:_reviewer_redact_names

chunk_findings.detail: The regression only appends one fresh `gate.failed` against `.ddflow/reviewers.toml`. It never reloads state, never covers the `reviewers.py` return path, and does not rewrite the five shards that already contain the name, so those committed copies still publish it and a replay of `reviewer.configured` is untested.

chunk_findings.detail: `_is_local_endpoint` only exact-matches `localhost` and `localdomain`, so a loopback name that is not a literal IP still skips redaction. Given `base_url = "http://reviewer.localhost:8000/v1"` (RFC 6761) or `http://devbox.localdomain:11434/v1`, `hostname` is neither of those two strings, does not end with `.local`/`.internal`/`.lan`/`.home.arpa`, and `ipaddress.ip_address` raises, so the function returns False. `_reviewer_redact_names` then omits that reviewer's `name` and `model`, and a `gate.failed` evidence payload still writes `local-reviewer-f8f8` into the shard. The regression test only configures `http://[REDACTED:ipv4]:8000/v1`, so this path stays green.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/log/_eventlog.py:_is_local_endpoint

chunk_findings.detail: The new module claims a local reviewer name never reaches the committed log, but this test appends `reviewer.configured` with subject `local-reviewer-f8f8` and asserts `"subject":"local-reviewer-f8f8"` is in the shard. That event is an EventLog write under `.ddflow/events`, the same committed shards the bug is about, and redaction does not touch the subject. `test_the_unapproved_reviewer_hint_reads_the_subject_not_the_redacted_evidence` already resolves the hint from in-memory `reviewer_writes`, so persisting the service name in the pushed subject is not required for that readback and leaves the leak in place.
